newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at record after brush with 700.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at record after brush with 700.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at their third consecutive record high on Tuesday, boosted by strong fourth quarter results and plans to sell some units announced by Anglo-Dutch foods to detergents combine Unilever.

The AEX index of 25 leading Dutch shares crossed the 700 level for the first time with a brief foray to 700.31 before settling back to close 3.68 points higher at a record 698.72. The previous intra-day high of 698.21 was set on Monday.
"We did get across 700 but Wall Street was up 18 points at the time and we only stayed there for two minutes," said one dealer, noting the market had been led all day by Unilever.
Dealers said the market undertone was becoming difficult to predict, with a long-awaited consolidation to gains since the AEX started the year at 648 stubbornly refusing to materialise.
"At the moment the main focus is on further results expected later this week. No-one is expecting much of a push from Philips (full year) figures on Thursday," said another dealer.

"Everyone is expecting a consolidation, there are some bearish positions opening up in the futures market, but no-one wants to make a move," he said. Chart analysts on Monday said they saw more upside potential in the AEX as more money flows into the market with first resistance at 700 on the AEX.
"The market doesn't want to consolidate, although it's not that keen on going ahead decisively," said another dealer.
Dealers said Unilever had accounted for the bulk of today's gain. "If it hadn't been for the big rise in Unilever we might actually be down on the day," said one.

Unilever closed 17.90 guilders up at 331.30 on news fourth quarter net profit at current exchange rates jumped to 1.15 billion guilders from 690 million, at the top end of analysts' forecasts which ranged from 869 million to 1.15 billion. News it was putting its speciality chemicals units up for sale was also taken as a positive sign of its intent to grow core businesses.
